delivery.replay: Follow metric-series nextCursor until complete is true or expose an incomplete tail.
delivery.resume: Send the last durable event cursor as since; apply only retained metricDeltas from each atomic frame.
delivery.terminal: A final frame closes live delivery while the completed metric series remains replayable.

requests.purpose: Credential-safe activation doctor only; not part of the render hot path.

unavailable: Both teams need independently retained win-probability series; Aura never infers the missing side.
Score margin is unavailable when either team lacks a retained score series.
Inning or period bands render only from retained categorical state.
A stopped metric cursor exposes metric_series_tail instead of claiming a complete replay.
Connected errors never replace real partial data with fixture values.

instructions: Render auraGamePulseFixture first; it needs no API key and demonstrates the paired probability, margin, and period contracts.
Create the browser-safe client with createAuraLiveScoreboardClient(). Keep AURA_API_KEY or RAPIDAPI_KEY and RAPIDAPI_HOST only in the copied server route environment.
Call useAuraGamePulse({ client, gameId, mode: 'live' }) and pass the returned state to <AuraGamePulse state={state} />.
Use mode 'replay' for a retained final. The loader follows every metric-series cursor before marking the model complete.
Keep both teams on the probability surface around the fixed 50 percent midpoint. Never replace the pair with one team plus an inferred visual unless the Aura object contains both retained series.
Treat inning or quarter as categorical bands, never as a numeric metric line. Unavailable probability, score, period, stale, error, and partial-tail states must remain explicit.
Styling and layout are customer-owned source. The copied data client remains intentionally Aura-specific; do not replace it with an interchangeable sports-data provider abstraction.
customization: Change colors, typography, spacing, chart height, and motion without changing probability or period semantics.
Add compatible team, player, or market series as overlays using their declared unit and semantic axis.
Move team labels or inspector placement while preserving both probability values and accessible chart labels.
